lead.title: OxyPrem wins MDR CE marking for NOAH, its tissue oximeter for premature babies' brains
lead.deck: Zurich start-up OxyPrem says NOAH, a near-infrared tissue oximetry system that continuously and non-invasively tracks tissue oxygenation (including the preterm infant's brain), is CE-marked under MDR 2017/745 and available across Europe. The reusable NOAH Sensor Small uses more than 10 wavelengths and reports 2.5% accuracy (ARMS) in neonates.

milestone.title: NeuroLF becomes the first dedicated brain PET accredited by EARL
milestone.summary: The ultra-compact NeuroLF PET, built only for brain imaging, is the first brain PET system accredited under the EARL programme (EANM Research Ltd.), which standardises PET imaging across European centres. The accreditation was carried out by the nuclear medicine department of LMU Klinikum Munich, where the unit is installed.
milestone.why: EARL accreditation makes measurements comparable from one centre to another: it is what allows a compact brain PET to be used in multicentre neurodegeneration trials outside the large departments equipped with whole-body PET/CT.

brefsEurope.title: MindMaze: at home, motor-training dose triples (Vibra review, 177 episodes)
brefsEurope.summary: Uncontrolled retrospective review published by the company: 177 rehab episodes in 172 adults (mostly post-stroke) at 4 Vibra Healthcare sites, 84% of active training done without direct supervision, significant gains in independence, balance, mobility and cognition. MindMotion Lite, a tablet version, is expected by end-2026.

brefsIntl.title: Sirona Medical raises $40M Series D for its cloud radiology platform RadOS
brefsIntl.summary: Round led by Avidity Partners, with 8VC and GreatPoint Ventures. RadOS combines PACS, reporting, viewer and worklist; Sirona is targeting international markets (UK, Europe) through Sirona Global.

brefsIntl.title: EndoQuest Robotics hires Jared Eben (ex-HCA Healthcare) as chief commercial officer
brefsIntl.summary: Former VP of robotics, AI and neuroscience at HCA, with stints at Proximie and Auris Health. EndoQuest is preparing an FDA De Novo request for its flexible surgical system (PARADIGM trial fully enrolled in July 2026) and aims for a US launch next year.

word.definition: A non-invasive optical technique that sends near-infrared light through tissue to continuously estimate its oxygenation (tissue saturation, StO₂).

how.t: The sensor, placed on the skin (e.g. a newborn's forehead), emits light at several near-infrared wavelengths.
Oxygenated and deoxygenated haemoglobin absorb these wavelengths differently; the backscattered light is picked up by the detectors.
An algorithm derives tissue saturation (StO₂), displayed continuously.

word.why: NIRS is the common building block of neonatal brain monitoring and wearable fNIRS headsets. The barrier is regulatory and clinical (MDR, accuracy in newborns): OxyPrem has just cleared it, while players like Artinis or Kernel take the same physics toward research and neuroscience.
